title: Teaching, methods and absorption
summary: Why he does not teach: a teacher inspires rather than gives specifics.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Were you able to incorporate any of the things you learned
in charts and various things you did for Benny?

One doesn't learn that. It's a process of absorption and the way you think, and what I learned I really don't know. I couldn't enumerate it today, I wouldn't begin to tell you what I knew. I don't teach because I don't feel secure I think people want to know specifics and I don't know that I'm prepared. I can't give specifics to someone else without drawing up, which you have seen me do too often here; if they want something else, I don't know. I think the function of a teacher, the way I see it is, to inspire somehow someone to seek his own path and his own levels, whatever that may be.
Techniques are too often self serving, they certainly have time
limits on them. They work for a given period and not much more.
You can look for general principles, and I think they are there; I keep looking and I'm not so sure that I ever do find any though.

If there is anything such as a general principle, it's more osmosis and too diffuse to verbalize. The moment you verbalize it, to begin isolating certain segments of it that are convenient, and you're allowing to escape probably the most important part of what was happening.
